performance-suite-seconds.noisePolicy:
One warmup is discarded; three isolated runs are measured; the median must remain at or below the ratcheted maximum.

Raised 21.0 -> 24.0 on 2026-08-14, calibrated from CI rather than from a dev machine. The 21.0 ceiling was set from a dev median of ~19.8s and sat INSIDE the CI distribution: 18 samples across 6 runners over two days ranged 20.352-21.439s (peak-to-peak 5.2%), and observed CI medians included 20.618, 20.692, 21.209 and 22.391s with individual samples to 22.962s. The gate therefore failed on which runner it landed on rather than on any regression, and six controlled same-commit dispatches went 2/3 green on two different branches identically.

24.0 sits ~12% above the highest observed CI sample (21.439s) instead of at roughly the 50th percentile of the distribution. The metric itself is sound and is NOT startup-dominated: startup is 3.8% of the suite on a dev machine and 7.3% on CI, so the measurement is 92-96% compute, and its run-to-run CV (~1.6%) is the lowest of any signal in this suite.

Prior precedent for moving this number with evidence: #942 raised 20.0 -> 21.0, and cut test cost first (one shared index build instead of three) before moving the ceiling. Order matters: cheaper tests first, ceiling second. No test cost was added here, so no such reduction was available.

This ceiling does NOT address #965's runner terminations (exit 143), which are unexplained and are what actually blocked v0.13.2. See docs/plans/performance-gate-strategy.md.

Raised 24.0 -> 48.0 on 2026-11-21 for the 0.30.0 release, calibrated from CI by the same rule (~12% above the highest observed CI sample). The 0.30.0 release dry run (run 44917750117) measured 43.235 s warmup and 42.817, 42.970, 42.627 s measured (median 42.817 s, highest 42.970 s); 0.29.0's release run had a 12.304 s median. Two causes, both recorded: the suite grew 28 -> 40 tests in 0.30, and IndexPerformanceTests' index build went from 0.38 s to ~10 s (paid twice: fixture and test) because the effect pass the index runs per module now does Roslyn-backed operator, indexer and dotted-chain binding. The policy says cheaper tests first; that reduction is the index-build fix tracked in #1738, which lowers this ceiling again. Raising it here keeps the gate catching further growth instead of failing on a measured, attributed and filed cost.

Lowered 48.0 -> 41.0 on 2026-11-22 for #1738 (the index build no longer re-binds each module's C# image, and effect summaries scan declarations instead of building a call graph; index and CLI output are byte-identical), calibrated from CI by the same rule (~12% above the highest observed CI sample). Nine performance.yml dispatches of the final commit measured medians of 22.198, 22.880, 25.498, 27.762, 28.146, 32.573, 35.066, 35.283 and 35.711 s; the 27 measured samples ranged 21.502-36.637 s, and 41.0 is ~12% above 36.637. (One further dispatch failed DataflowAnalysis_ComplexCFG_IsTimingSmokeTest at 60.9 ms against its 25 ms smoke budget, in code this change does not touch; its rerun passed and is one of the nine.) Same-day dispatches of main (0.30.0 code) measured medians of 33.881, 33.983, 42.730, 35.213 and 43.373 s, and the 2026-11-21 nightly measured 46.512-47.470 s. IndexBuildStaysWithinItsBudget measured 3.10-5.56 s on the branch against 7.68-12.2 s on main. The slowest runner class seen so far ran main at ~47 s; if the branch's ratio to main on matching runners (~0.8) holds there, it would measure ~38-39 s, inside 41.0 but with only ~5% headroom. The index build is still ~8-15x its 0.29 cost (0.38 s); what remains is mostly the symbol index's single Roslyn binding of each module's image.

Lowered 41.0 -> 40.0 on 2026-11-23 for the second #1738 reduction (cheaper AST walks, snapshot hashing and identity parses; index and CLI output byte-identical to 0.30.0). Eight performance.yml dispatches of that commit measured medians of 25.195, 26.982, 31.509, 32.073, 32.770, 32.905, 33.310 and 33.506 s; the 24 measured samples ranged 25.044-33.664 s. Same-day dispatches of main (the first reduction) measured medians of 26.621 and 34.597 s. The usual rule (~12% above the highest sample) gives 37.7, but no dispatch landed on the slowest runner class seen so far (0.30.0 at 47.284 s, nightly 2026-11-21). Scaling the first reduction's estimate for that class (~38-39 s) by this change's 3-5% suite gain puts this code at ~36.5-37.5 s there, so 40.0 keeps ~7-9% headroom on that class and is 19% above the highest observed sample. IndexBuildStaysWithinItsBudget measured 3.27-4.89 s against main's 3.89-4.91 s on the same day. The index build is still ~8-13x its 0.29 cost (0.38 s); most of the rest is the symbol index's Roslyn binding of each module's C# image, which is what its answers come from.

Lowered 40.0 -> 38.0 on 2026-11-23 for the third #1738 reduction (the index build's per-module work runs on all cores: the source-call bindings prewarm, the registry's projections, the shared image's parse check, the effect summaries and the identity store's declaration parses; index and multi-file compile output byte-identical to the sequential build). Six performance.yml dispatches of that commit (b6e18066a; runs 45297923847, 45297937618, 45297948983, 45297959640, 45297971469, 45297984084) measured medians of 18.590, 23.918, 29.443, 29.896, 30.273 and 30.389 s; the 18 measured samples ranged 18.410-30.526 s. Two same-hour dispatches of main (8046caef2; runs 45297994168, 45298002910) measured medians of 31.133 and 32.108 s, so on runners of similar speed the suite is ~3-8% faster. The usual rule (~12% above the highest sample) gives 34.2, but again no dispatch landed on the slowest runner class seen so far (0.30.0 at 47.284 s, nightly 2026-11-21). Scaling the second reduction's estimate for that class (~36.5-37.5 s) by this change's ~5% suite gain puts this code at ~34.7-35.6 s there, so 38.0 keeps ~7-9% headroom on that class and is 24% above the highest observed sample. The index build is still well above its 0.29 cost: locally (Apple silicon, 14 cores, heavily loaded host) the warm fixture-10k build has a fastest run of 1.27 s against 0.21 s for 0.29.0 and 1.50 s for main. What remains is sequential by construction: the symbol index's bind of each module, the effect pass (whose binds read modules earlier passes rewrote) and the identity store.
